scope: Passive inspection of saved source, CFG, processing, Task correspondence and compiled annotation. No semantic model, compiler, propagation, DOE, Skill or replay executed. Not a source-review receipt. Initial materials may be superseded by bounded repair.
boundary_locator_caveat: 13 physical remote source sites. The lexical join is ambiguous at Search Console because ir_171 builds the request and ir_173 calls the remote; operation and CFG inspection identifies ir_173 as the remote consumer. No runtime boundary coverage is claimed.

findings.summary: Six explicit CFG client inputs and seven inline client values do not reach their remote call or location binding.
findings.evidence: All listed compiled remote locations have operand_refs=[] and no actual client/cache binding. Explicit client operands have zero value references in their IR semantics. Inline cases yield h, with zero h value references. ga_cache is a distinct runtime_context; service locations are fixed remote names. Completion guards retain possible construction failure, but do not preserve which authenticated handle is used.
findings.implication: Current remote semantics cannot by these edges establish actual authenticated client identity. This is a source-model omission, not proof of a published deletion, missing network execution, or loss of every credential/control demand.

findings.summary: Eight inlined report-wrapper records bind/save the raw modeled ga_report receive output without an explicit response projection or a declared normalized-return adapter.
findings.challenge_and_limit: The actual high-level source callee getPageViews (and peer wrappers) already returns ReportResponse; direct binding would be correct if the modeled call represented that wrapper. These saved records instead build the SDK request and call the shared remote ga_report location named Google Analytics Data API BetaAnalyticsDataClient.runReport. That same location in ir_099 and ir_106 has explicit tuple[0] selection. No location signature or adapter declares that the eight calls alone return a normalized first element. The receive output is abstract and no actual tuple-valued runtime output has been observed, so this is not counted as eight proven wrong runtime values.
findings.resolution: Declare and source-bind a normalized wrapper-return interface, or represent the SDK response-to-first-report projection explicitly. Source review must determine which abstraction is intended.

positive_checks.limits: Matching request IDs does not establish receiver identity. The previous specific date-range-as-report misbinding does not recur at these 19 sites; no claim that all request, storage or output semantics are correct.
